paper.title_en: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
paper.abstract_en: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. With unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional MCMC posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. When marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. Under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. We test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. We find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. Finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a LISA global fit.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该文提出基于Simformer（transformer结合扩散/流匹配）的LISA随机分量分离模拟推断框架，处理非高斯瞬变、数据间隙与非等臂等现实特征，并用重要性重加权的局部化模拟校准检验后验覆盖率，方法学较为扎实且对PTA/随机引力波背景分析有直接参考价值；属于空间引力波随机背景数据处理，故归入pta主题。
decision.title_zh: 扩散假设：面向真实LISA随机分量分离的物理感知模拟推断
decision.abstract_zh: 对激光干涉空间天线（LISA）所观测的大量源进行同时全局拟合推断，依赖于对其随机成分的精确建模：仪器噪声、银河系前景，以及天体物理或随机引力波背景（SGWB）。非高斯瞬变和数据间隙等现实特征对传统基于似然的流程构成挑战，这为模拟推断（SBI）增强传统分析创造了机会。在此，我们提出一个用于LISA随机成分分离的SBI框架，它建立在Simformer之上——一个用扩散或流匹配训练、通过物理感知嵌入接收完整时延干涉测量互谱矩阵的transformer。我们在包含强前景和微弱幂律SGWB的11.6天模拟数据集上逐步放宽标准简化假设。在不等臂和逐链路噪声自由度下，网络在重要性重加权后与17维MCMC后验相匹配；完整互谱将每条链路的光学计量噪声幅度约束到$1\%$。当对瞬变或大质量黑洞双星瞬变进行边缘化时，估计误差在瞬变信噪比高达数百时仍保持平坦，而忽略它们则会严重偏置似然拟合。在时变样条噪声水平、现实瞬变率和长达一天的间隙下，后验覆盖率在$\sim 10^4$次模拟中保持标称或保守。我们通过引入一种新颖的重要性加权局部化模拟校准检验，在给定观测的局部邻域内检验覆盖率。我们发现，在较简单的情形下，流匹配的校准略优于扩散，并观察到物理感知模板输入带来适度增益。最后，我们概述了这些网络如何为LISA全局拟合的噪声块和随机块提供初始化。
